天同.intro: Tian Tong is the star of ease and good fortune. It stands for enjoying life and getting along with people. It dislikes conflict, likes to make the people around it comfortable, and knows how to find small pleasures in ordinary days. In whichever palace it sits, you tend to be more easygoing and relaxed about that area. Its strengths are a soft attitude, good relationships, and knowing when you have enough. What to watch: when you want stability too much, you may keep putting off decisions you need to make.
天同.personality: You have a good temper and are easy to be around, often the friend who eases the mood. You care about quality of life: eating well, sleeping well, being comfortable. You have little guile and tend to trust people. Where you can get stuck: under pressure you want to step away first, and things grow bigger the longer they wait. Let small matters take their course, but give big ones a time when you will face them.
天同.love: In love you are gentle and accepting, and you like a relationship that is easy and not tense all the time. Watch for swallowing your dissatisfaction to avoid a fight. Saying what you feel early is easier to deal with than letting it pile up.
天同.work: Work that involves service, caring for others, or dealing with people suits you, and colleagues usually find you easy to work with. If your pace runs slow, set yourself a few small goals and move forward one step at a time.

廉貞.intro: Lian Zhen is a star full of tension, carrying both principle and passion. It values rules, has strong likes and dislikes, and puts a great deal of itself into people and matters. In whichever palace it sits, you hold strong opinions and care a lot about right and wrong in that area. Lian Zhen's energy varies widely, and it looks very different with different stars. What they share: you give everything when you commit, and you can also fixate more easily when stuck.
廉貞.personality: You have your own yardstick inside, and it is hard for you to pretend you didn't see something you can't accept. You are ambitious and work to win what you want. You look calm outside, but your inner feelings are rich. Where you can get stuck: you demand too much of yourself and others, and a small mistake stays on your mind for a long time. Learning to tell which things are worth holding firm on and which can be let go will make life much lighter.
廉貞.love: In love you give deeply, and you care whether your partner is faithful and treats you sincerely. Watch for possessiveness that leaves the other person feeling stifled. Giving each other a little space can actually bring you closer.
廉貞.work: Work that calls for principle, strategy, or public-relations skill suits you, and you can find a way through complicated situations. Watch that personal likes and dislikes don't sway your judgment. Try to address the issue, not the person.

天府.intro: Tian Fu is the star that keeps the storehouse. It stands for preserving what has been built, accumulating, and looking after the whole picture. It is not in a hurry, likes to lay a solid foundation step by step, and manages the resources in hand well. In whichever palace it sits, you have a strong need for security there and want to get it settled properly. Its strength is being steady and reliable, which puts people at ease. What to watch: when you want stability too much, you may hesitate too long over new opportunities.
天府.personality: You come across as reliable and sensible. You plan your work and don't like taking needless risks. You value a secure life and look after the people around you. You are polite to others, but you have your own mind. Where you can get stuck: caring too much about what others think, or holding to the status quo and missing the time to change. Trying a small change now and then will not shake your foundation.
天府.love: In love you are steady and devoted to home. You want security in the relationship and are willing to plan for the two of your futures. Watch for treating care as control. Sometimes what the other person needs is simply to be trusted, so loosening your grip is better.
天府.work: Administration, management, and work that needs long-term tending suit you. You are good at protecting results and using resources just right. When a new approach comes up, try it on a small scale first, then decide whether to switch fully.

太陰.intro: Tai Yin stands for the Moon. It is a gentle, delicate star that values feeling. It governs inner security and the sense of home, and it is also linked to saving and accumulating. In whichever palace it sits, you take that area to heart and are easily moved by emotion there. Tai Yin's condition depends on whether it sits in a daytime or nighttime position. When bright it is warm and graceful. When dimmer, there is more on your mind and you need to take better care of yourself.
太陰.personality: You are perceptive and quickly notice shifts in other people's moods. You value beauty and atmosphere and like to live with a sense of quality. You don't show much, but you think a great deal. Where you can get stuck: keeping feelings bottled up until you can't bear it and they all come out at once. Talking with someone you trust, or writing things down to sort them out, can make your heart lighter.
太陰.love: In love you are gentle and considerate, remember your partner's small habits, and need to be treated with the same care. Watch for expecting the other person to guess what you mean. Say what you want directly so they know how to come closer.
太陰.work: Work that needs care, aesthetic sense, or patient accumulation suits you. You work steadily and deliver good quality. Don't dwell on a remark or two. Focus on what you do well.

貪狼.intro: Tan Lang is a star with strong desire and talent. It stands for curiosity, socializing, and enthusiasm for life. It has wide interests, learns quickly, and knows how to warm up a room. In whichever palace it sits, you want to experience and try more in that area. Its strengths are versatility and wide popularity. What to watch: when you want too much, your energy scatters and each thing gets done only halfway.
貪狼.personality: You like new things and are interested in food, entertainment, and all kinds of skills. You chat easily with people and are often the one who lifts the mood in a group. When you want to do something, you find a way. Where you can get stuck: enthusiasm that fades fast, or saying yes to too many invitations on a whim. Pick one or two things you truly care about and stay with them, and your talent will be seen more clearly.
貪狼.love: In love you are passionate and charming, good at creating surprises so that being with you is never dull. Watch for the quiet stretch after the newness fades. Putting your effort into tending everyday life together will make the relationship steadier.
貪狼.work: Sales, marketing, creative work, or work that relies on connections suits you. You learn fast and adapt well. Don't take on too many projects at once. Focusing on a few is how you build bigger results.

巨門.intro: Ju Men is a star tied to eloquence and critical thinking. It stands for digging to the root of things and the ability to influence others through words. It likes to get things clear and is good at spotting problems others missed. In whichever palace it sits, you think a lot and have much to say in that area. Its strengths are analysis and expression. What to watch: when you speak too bluntly, people may feel they are being picked apart.
巨門.personality: You are sharp-eyed and often see right away what is off. You speak in an orderly way and rarely lose a debate. On things you care about, you check again and again and don't easily accept the surface. Where you can get stuck: many doubts in your mind can lead to misunderstandings between people. When you raise a question, adding "I just want to understand" makes the other person less likely to feel doubted.
巨門.love: In love you value communication. You want to talk things out and dislike the silent treatment. Watch for arguing your reasons too fully in a fight. The other person needs to feel understood first, and reasons go over better afterward.
巨門.work: Work that needs eloquence, research, or professional analysis suits you, such as teaching, consulting, or research. Besides pointing out problems, remember to sincerely recognize what others do well when the moment is right.

天相.intro: Tian Xiang is a Resource star. It stands for coordination, fairness, and the ability to get things done for others. It knows how to find balance among different people and values order and courtesy. In whichever palace it sits, you want to handle that area thoroughly so everyone can get by. Its strengths are being steady and reliable. It is strongly shaped by the stars around it: when its neighbors run smoothly, it does too, and when they are stuck, it is put in a bind as well.
天相.personality: You are courteous and methodical, and are often trusted with important tasks. You value fairness and dislike seeing anyone get the short end. You look after the mood of a group and are glad to offer friends advice. Where you can get stuck: caring so much about everyone's feelings that you can't voice your own opinion. Stating your position now and then helps everyone see what you think.
天相.love: In love you are considerate and committed, treating your partner's matters as your own. Watch for going along with everything and putting your own needs last. Both people in a relationship should be cared for.
天相.work: Administration, HR, coordination, or work that depends on trust suits you. With you there, the team runs smoothly. Don't clean up too many of other people's messes. When you need to say no, say it gently.

紫微.intro: Zi Wei is often called the Emperor star, and of the fourteen main stars it has the strongest sense of being the "master." On a chart it stands for the side of you that wants to hold the direction and make decisions for those around you. In whichever palace it sits, you care a lot about whether your word counts there. Zi Wei needs help to do well. With Zuo Fu, You Bi, Tian Fu or Tian Xiang in the same palace or among the three connected palaces, it's more like leading a team. With none around, it easily turns into carrying everything alone.
紫微.personality: Your first impression is usually steady and measured, and you don't like being told what to do. You tend to look at the big picture first, then decide whether the details need your attention. Your pride is strong. When respected, you give willingly. When you feel looked down on, you quietly pull away. The snag is valuing face more than what's actually needed. Sometimes saying "I need help" gets things moving faster.
紫微.love: In love, you want to be appreciated, and you tend to look after your partner and arrange everything for the two of you. But after a while, looking after can turn into deciding for them. Try asking "What do you want to do?" more often, and the relationship will feel much lighter.
紫微.work: You suit roles that call for coordinating and making the final call. You lead with presence, and people are willing to listen. The biggest risk is having the position but no one to share the work. Gather trusted partners early. You'll go further than by holding up the whole stage alone.

天機.intro: Among the fourteen main stars, Tian Ji is the most like the brain. It governs thinking, planning and change. It turns quickly, likes working out the reasons behind things, and is good at seeing which step in a process could run more smoothly. In whichever palace it sits, you think hard and love to adjust. The upside is quick reactions and plenty of ideas. Watch for overthinking, which can leave you circling in place and slow to act.
天機.personality: You're thoughtful and observant. Often you've thought of the next step before others finish speaking. You like learning new things and tire quickly of repetition. You tend to run several outcomes in your head before deciding what to do. The snag is worrying too much and getting tired before anything has happened. Give yourself a deadline: once you've thought this far, start. It will ease things a lot.
天機.love: In love, you value easy conversation and like someone you can discuss things with and share new discoveries. But when you overthink, you may read several layers into one remark. If you have a question, ask directly. It takes less effort than guessing.
天機.work: Planning, analysis and any work that uses your head to solve problems suit you well. You're good at improving processes and finding new methods. Watch out for starting too many things at once. Finish one before opening the next.

太陽.intro: Tai Yang is a star that shines outward. It stands for warmth, giving, and the side of you that wants to be seen. It likes taking care of others and cares whether what it does has meaning. In whichever palace it sits, you're especially willing to commit and want to show people something good. Tai Yang's state depends on whether it sits in a daytime or nighttime position. When bright, it is generous and open. When dimmer, it's harder: you give a lot but may not be noticed.
太陽.personality: You're straightforward and usually say what's on your mind. It's hard for you to ignore unfairness. You like liveliness and are willing to take the lead. You're loyal to friends and often think of others first. The snag is giving so much that you forget you get tired too, or expecting others to respond with the same warmth. It's fine to step back and rest now and then.
太陽.love: In love, you're generous and take the initiative. You like looking after your partner and are glad to introduce them to the people around you. Note that your way of giving may not be what they want. Asking what they truly need is more caring than just giving more.
太陽.work: Work that faces people, drives projects or leads a team suits you well. You have drive and the ability to rally others. Be clear about credit and division of work so you don't become the one who takes on everything.

武曲.intro: Wu Qu is a Wealth star and also a very practical, action-oriented star. It values results, lets numbers and achievements speak, and acts decisively without dragging things out. In whichever palace it sits, you're especially serious and want to earn your place through your own effort. Wu Qu's strength is execution and endurance, seeing a task through from start to finish. Watch for focusing so hard on the goal that you overlook how people around you feel.
武曲.personality: You work crisply, do what you say, and dislike empty talk. You hold yourself to a high standard and hope others keep up with your speed. You may seem hard on the outside, but inside you take promises seriously. The snag is speaking too bluntly, so a well-meant remark sounds like an order. Saying one considerate thing before the main point makes a big difference.
武曲.love: In love, you aren't much for sweet talk. You'd rather care through action, like handling a troublesome task for your partner. But sometimes they need a word of affirmation. Saying aloud that you care now and then will warm the relationship.
武曲.work: Finance, management, and work that needs execution and a head for numbers suit you well. You can bear pressure and hardship. Watch that you don't push yourself too hard. Sharing the work and keeping some energy in reserve lets you go the distance.

天梁.intro: Tian Liang is a star of shelter, standing for care, protection, and the wisdom of an elder. It likes to help people think things through, holds firm principles, and can see further down the road. In whichever palace it sits, you feel an extra sense of responsibility for those matters and want to hold things up for others. Its strengths are maturity, reliability, and a steady nerve. What to watch: when you care for others too much, it can turn into doing too much for them, or getting used to cleaning up after them.
天梁.personality: You have a mature outlook, and even when young you were often the person others came to talk things over with. You value principles, your words carry weight, and you stay calm when trouble comes. You like reasoning things through and are glad to share what you've learned. Where you can get stuck: offering too much well-meant advice, so the other person feels lectured. Listen first, then ask whether they'd like your view. You'll be better received.
天梁.love: In love you are dependable and accepting, and you take good care of your partner. When they hit a hard moment, you're often the first person they think of. Watch for treating your partner as someone to be protected. Relating more as equals helps the relationship last.
天梁.work: Work that calls for expertise, care, or oversight suits you, such as education, counseling, or management, where you help people grow. Watch for carrying everything yourself. Let go a little, and let others learn to do it on their own.

七殺.intro: Qi Sha is a general star with strong drive, standing for starting new things, decisiveness, and the courage to face a challenge. It isn't afraid of change, and the harder the situation, the more fight it stirs up. In whichever palace it sits, you especially want to charge ahead and make your own decisions in those matters. Its strengths are action and nerve. What to watch: when you rush too fast, you may act before you've weighed things up, and then spend effort cleaning up afterward.
七殺.personality: You are independent and do what you say you'll do, and you dislike being tied down. Pressure tends to sharpen you, and you are willing to take risks. You are loyal to your friends. You may seem hard to approach, but your heart is warm. Where you can get stuck: saying things too harshly when your temper rises, or charging ahead alone with your head down. Pausing for three seconds before you act can save a lot of trouble.
七殺.love: In love you are direct and bold. When you like someone, you go after them and don't play games with vagueness. Watch for holding the other person to your own speed. A relationship moves forward with two people, so sometimes slow down and wait for them.
七殺.work: Work that means breaking new ground or handling sudden change suits you, such as starting a business, sales, or tackling hard projects. Watch for this: after a sprint ends, plan some rest, and tie up the details left behind.

破軍.intro: Po Jun is a star that breaks up old arrangements and starts over, standing for change, risk-taking, and restlessness with the status quo. When it sees something unreasonable, it wants to step in and fix it, and it isn't afraid to begin again from scratch. In whichever palace it sits, you are especially likely to go through big shifts in those matters, or to push for change yourself. Its strengths are boldness and creativity. What to watch: when you change things too fast, the old is torn down before the new is built, and the stretch in between can be hard.
破軍.personality: You don't like things staying the same, and you are curious about new methods and new surroundings. You dare to think and act, and are often the first to stand up and say, "Let's try a different way." You hold firmly to what you believe in. Where you can get stuck: patience runs short, and you want to switch tracks before finishing something. Give yourself a milestone, and decide whether to switch only after you reach it. That is steadier.
破軍.love: In love you are passionate and genuine, clear in your likes and dislikes, and you put your whole heart in when you care. Watch for wanting to overturn everything at the first dissatisfaction. Many problems can be adjusted slowly, and it's not too late to talk first and decide afterward.
破軍.work: Work that involves innovation, reform, or starting from zero suits you, and you can carve out a new path in the middle of chaos. Watch for this: before you make a change, keep a way back, and take the pace of the people beside you into account.

empty.命宮: No main star in the Life Palace doesn't mean you have no personality. It means you tend to adjust to your surroundings. To read it, we borrow the main stars from the opposite Travel Palace. Their qualities are yours too, just softer and more dependent on the occasion. The upside is flexibility and quick adaptation. The snag is that you sometimes can't say what you want, so give yourself time to ask.
empty.兄弟: When the Siblings Palace is empty, we borrow the main stars from the opposite Friends Palace to read your siblings, peers and the people around you. How you get along with your brothers and sisters is often much like how you make friends outside the family. These relationships aren't a fixed shape. They change with each person's stage of life. Reaching out when you have time is more real than waiting for the other person to do it first.
empty.夫妻: With no main star in the Spouse Palace, we borrow the main stars from the opposite Career Palace. What you expect from a partner is often tied to how you approach work. When you're busy, love easily goes to the back. When things go smoothly, you want your partner to understand your pace. The shape of the relationship is something you can work out together slowly, without settling it at the start.
empty.子女: With the Children Palace empty, we borrow the main stars from the opposite Property Palace. This palace also covers how you lead, teach and create. The mood at home and how you arrange your living space directly affect your bond with younger people and with your work. Get your own life steady first, and you'll have more room to spare when guiding others.
empty.財帛: With no main star in the Wealth Palace, we borrow the main stars from the opposite Well-being Palace. How you earn and spend is closely tied to how comfortable you feel inside. When your mood is steady, your money rhythm is steady. When you're upset, you may spend to soothe yourself. Keeping clear track of income and spending helps more than chasing one big gain.
empty.疾厄: With the Health Palace empty, we borrow the main stars from the opposite Parents Palace. This palace speaks only of daily routine, stress and pace of life. Your pace is often shaped by family habits or elders' expectations, and you may find yourself following someone else's schedule without noticing. Setting aside a stretch of rest that belongs only to you works better than pushing through.
empty.遷移: With no main star in the Travel Palace, we borrow the main stars from the opposite Life Palace. You are much the same outside as at home and don't put on a different face on purpose. When you go out or change settings, you mostly rely on your own nature. In a new place, watch for a while first, then decide how to fit in. You'll feel more at ease.
empty.交友: With the Friends Palace empty, we borrow the main stars from the opposite Siblings Palace. You make friends much like you treat family and peers: once you know someone, you're sincere. Your circle may not be large, and it tends to change with each stage of life. You don't need to force every friendship to last. Keep the ones that feel comfortable to both of you.
empty.官祿: With no main star in the Career Palace, we borrow the main stars from the opposite Spouse Palace. The direction of your work is often shaped by the people closest to you, and you're especially motivated when someone supports you. Your work life is flexible and may not follow one road to the end. When you face a choice, ask yourself what kind of life you want. The answer gets clearer.
empty.田宅: With the Property Palace empty, we borrow the main stars from the opposite Children Palace. Your feeling about home is tied to how you care for the people around you and how you throw yourself into what you love. Where you live may change with your stage of life. There's no hurry to settle. For now, just make the space fit what you need today.
empty.福德: With no main star in the Well-being Palace, we borrow the main stars from the opposite Wealth Palace. Your ups and downs of mood are often linked to how comfortable your finances are. With steady income you loosen up. When you're busy earning, you forget to rest. It's worth finding one or two things that don't cost much and truly help you relax.
empty.父母: With the Parents Palace empty, we borrow the main stars from the opposite Health Palace. How you get along with elders and bosses is closely tied to your own routine and stress. When you're tired, one remark from them can sound harsh. Look after your own rhythm first, then talk about expectations. Communication will go much more smoothly.

palaces.官祿: Hua Quan in the Career Palace means you are ambitious at work. You suit taking on responsibility and leading a team, and you can make decisions under pressure. When a promotion or a big project comes along, accept it graciously and don't be too modest.
palaces.田宅: Hua Quan in the Property Palace means you like to handle household matters yourself, and you have strong ideas about your living space. Talk things over with your family and hear what each person needs, and home becomes a place where everyone is comfortable.
palaces.福德: Hua Quan in the Well-being Palace means you hold yourself to a high standard, and even leisure becomes something to excel at. You rarely switch off completely. Letting yourself do nothing now and then, with no plans, is an important way of taking care of yourself.
palaces.父母: Hua Quan in the Parents Palace means the elders or bosses around you tend to be opinionated and to manage a lot, so you often follow their arrangements. Treat their demands as suggestions to consider, and share your own concerns too. Communication will go more smoothly.
palaces.命宮: With Hua Quan in the Life Palace, you have opinions and boldness, you are used to making your own decisions, and others are easily persuaded by you. You are convincing when you lead. Remember to leave room to hear other people's ideas, and your team will pull together more.
palaces.兄弟: With Hua Quan in the Siblings Palace, you are often the one who decides among your peers, or else a sibling or partner has strong opinions. Respect each other's ways of doing things, and when you disagree, each step back a little first. You'll argue less.
palaces.夫妻: With Hua Quan in the Spouse Palace, one side of the relationship is often the more forceful one, the person who makes decisions. If the two of you spell out who handles what and which things to talk over together, the relationship will go more smoothly.
palaces.子女: With Hua Quan in the Children Palace, you hold younger people and students to higher standards, and you have a real method for guiding them. Let go at the right moments and let them try on their own. Give them some room to make mistakes, and they often grow in ways that surprise you.
palaces.財帛: With Hua Quan in the Wealth Palace, you like to be in control of money, you enjoy planning your own income and spending, and you are good at asking for fair pay. Strong follow-through is a good thing, but for large expenses, run the numbers once more and ask someone else before you decide.
palaces.疾厄: With Hua Quan in the Health Palace, you can hold up well and keep pushing even under heavy pressure, and people often think your energy never runs out. Because you can endure, you should set aside rest time for yourself and not stop only when you're completely worn out.
palaces.遷移: With Hua Quan in the Travel Palace, you act with boldness away from home, are easily pushed into a leading role, and don't get stage fright in unfamiliar settings. Working away from home, doing sales, or leading projects all let your abilities show well.
palaces.交友: With Hua Quan in the Friends Palace, your words carry weight in your circle of friends, or a few strong-minded friends surround you. When opinions clash, hear them out before you take a stand, and don't rush to decide who wins. The relationship will last longer.

權.plain: Hua Quan stands for strength, control, and taking the lead. In whichever palace it falls, you especially want to make your own decisions in those matters, and you are better able to push them forward. It gives boldness and follow-through, so you can take things on your shoulders. What to watch: when you use too much force, it can become domineering or stubborn. If you learn to balance leading with listening, Hua Quan is a fine driving force.

科.plain: Hua Ke stands for reputation, order, and helpful people. In whichever palace it falls, you handle that area with more grace and are more likely to be recognized for it. It doesn't bring resources as directly as Hua Lu does. Instead, it helps you be seen and trusted. Its influence is gentle and lasting, and it suits studying, exams, and building a good name. When you hit a difficulty, it often shows up as "someone happened to remind me."

palaces.命宮: Hua Ke in the Life Palace means you come across as refined and orderly. People trust how you speak and act, and you tend to leave a good impression at a first meeting. Your good name is an asset. Tend it with care and it will bring you opportunities.
palaces.兄弟: Hua Ke in the Siblings Palace means there is often someone among your siblings or peers who gives you sound advice, so you can go to them when something comes up. Exchanging ideas with them often helps you see things more clearly and completely.
palaces.夫妻: Hua Ke in the Spouse Palace means you admire a partner who is learned and well mannered. The two of you are reasonable and respectful with each other. The relationship tends to be calm, with few big ups and downs, and suits learning and growing together in daily life.
palaces.子女: Hua Ke in the Children Palace means younger people or students conduct themselves well, often making you proud and feel your effort was worthwhile. You also have a gift for teaching, guiding newcomers, and sharing experience, so look for more chances to use it.
palaces.財帛: Hua Ke in the Wealth Palace means you manage money in an orderly way and spend with a plan. Your credit is good, and people feel at ease dealing with you. Income mostly builds slowly through expertise and reputation, and steady effort tends to make things better over time.
palaces.疾厄: Hua Ke in the Health Palace means that under stress you know how to find ways to adjust, and you are fairly open to other people's advice. A regular routine works especially well for you, and a fixed bedtime is your best way to recharge.
palaces.遷移: Hua Ke in the Travel Palace means you make a good impression out in the world, are easily appreciated, and find errands outside go fairly smoothly. In a new environment, your skill and courtesy open doors and make people willing to give you more chances.
palaces.交友: Hua Ke in the Friends Palace means your friends tend to be cultured people you can learn from, and conversations often spark new ideas. Opportunities that come through friends are usually good ones, worth taking seriously and making the most of.
palaces.官祿: Hua Ke in the Career Palace means you value expertise and reputation at work, and you suit building your standing through credentials, work samples, or word of mouth. Keep learning and turn your results into something visible, and you will be better recognized.
palaces.田宅: Hua Ke in the Property Palace means your home has an orderly feel, and you like to keep your space tidy and tasteful. Home is a good place for you to recharge and study, and it is worth keeping a quiet corner for yourself.
palaces.福德: Hua Ke in the Well-being Palace means you enjoy reading, learning, or appreciating beautiful things, and your inner life is rich. These interests keep you balanced when you're busy. However busy you get, don't let them go completely. Save a little time for yourself.
palaces.父母: Hua Ke in the Parents Palace means the elders or bosses around you value good manners and reputation, and they often give you good examples and pointers. They are reasonable, so you can usually communicate well. When something comes up, don't hesitate to ask them for advice.

忌.plain: Hua Ji is often misunderstood as something bad. It is closer to "the place that takes the most care." In whichever palace your birth-year Hua Ji falls, you care especially deeply and find it hard to let go, and it needs the most time to tend. Because you care, it is often where you grow the most. Rather than fear it, treat it as a reminder: this matter deserves to be taken slowly. Don't rush for results. Handle it with care and it gets easier.

palaces.命宮: Hua Ji in the Life Palace means you ask a lot of yourself and often wonder whether you're doing well enough. The thing that takes the most care here is you. Learn to be a little gentler with yourself. You work harder than you think.
palaces.兄弟: Hua Ji in the Siblings Palace means dealing with siblings, peers, and partners takes the most care, and you often feel that what you give and what you get back are uneven. Say things plainly and keep accounts clear, and the relationship can actually grow closer.
palaces.夫妻: Hua Ji in the Spouse Palace means love is what you care about most and put the most care into, and you take every move your partner makes to heart. Communicate more and guess less, and give each other time to adjust. The relationship will grow steadier.
palaces.子女: Hua Ji in the Children Palace means you worry especially about younger people, students, or your own work, and you often can't let their matters go. Try trusting that they can handle things themselves. You will carry less worry and have more room to breathe.
palaces.財帛: Hua Ji in the Wealth Palace means money is where you put the most care, and you often worry whether you have enough or whether to spend. Keep clear records of income and spending and set aside a reserve. Your mind will settle, and you will feel readier to decide.
palaces.疾厄: Hua Ji in the Health Palace means your daily rhythm and stress are what you most need to look after, and when you get busy you easily forget yourself. Fixed rest times and attention to building fatigue are much easier than fixing things afterward.
palaces.遷移: Hua Ji in the Travel Palace means you tend to worry when you're out and about or changing environments, and unfamiliar places make you tense. Do some homework before you go and leave some flexibility in your plans. You will feel much more at ease and enjoy the trip more.
palaces.交友: Hua Ji in the Friends Palace means relationships are where you put the most care, and you often worry over your friends' troubles. You don't need to open your heart to everyone. Choose people worth trusting for close friendships, and keep a friendly distance with the rest.
palaces.官祿: Hua Ji in the Career Palace means work is what weighs most on your mind, and you often feel it's not good enough yet and could be better. Set clear milestones for yourself and acknowledge yourself when you reach them. The pressure will be easier to manage.
palaces.田宅: Hua Ji in the Property Palace means household matters and your living space are where you put the most care, and you often fret over chores or living arrangements. Divide chores clearly and adjust your living arrangements bit by bit, and home will feel more settled over time.
palaces.福德: Hua Ji in the Well-being Palace means your mind easily runs through a lot, relaxing takes practice for you, and even on days off you often carry things with you. Finding a way to quiet yourself will be a lesson that serves you for life.
palaces.父母: Hua Ji in the Parents Palace means dealing with elders and bosses takes the most care, and you often feel they don't quite understand you. Explain your thinking with a little more patience, and the distance between you will slowly close.

祿.plain: Hua Lu is the smoothest of the Four Transformations. It stands for resources, opportunities, and goodwill flowing toward that place. In whichever palace your birth-year Hua Lu falls, you handle those matters with more ease and are more likely to meet people willing to help. It is like water: it moves. So the point is to use it well and share it, not to grip it tight. When things go smoothly, remember to save a little for the future, so your good fortune keeps flowing.

palaces.命宮: With Hua Lu in the Life Palace, you were born with good rapport. You are easygoing, and people want to be near you. Many opportunities come through people, so going out and meeting more of them especially helps you. Don't forget to give back to those who have helped you.
palaces.兄弟: With Hua Lu in the Siblings Palace, siblings and peers are often a help to you. You look out for each other, and it's easier to speak up when you're struggling. Working together with partners brings more gains and more satisfaction than going it alone.
palaces.夫妻: With Hua Lu in the Spouse Palace, you are more likely to meet people in love who are compatible and generous, and being together feels easy. Your partner may also give you real help in daily life or at work. Remember to say thank you often.
palaces.子女: With Hua Lu in the Children Palace, you have good affinity with younger people and students. Guiding them is rewarding, and they are happy to be close to you. The effort you put into creative work or teaching is more likely to be noticed and liked.
palaces.財帛: With Hua Lu in the Wealth Palace, you tend to have more ways to earn, often have cash flowing in, and are more willing to spend on things that improve your life. Set aside a fixed part of your income, so the good times lay a base for the harder ones.
palaces.疾厄: With Hua Lu in the Health Palace, you naturally know how to enjoy life and look after yourself, and when your mood is good, your energy follows. Beyond eating and sleeping well, take care not to let your routine grow looser just because things feel comfortable.
palaces.遷移: With Hua Lu in the Travel Palace, you get along better with people outside than at home, and you often meet people willing to help when you go out. Changing environments or building a life elsewhere often opens up new possibilities. Don't confine yourself to a familiar circle.
palaces.交友: With Hua Lu in the Friends Palace, you have many friends and a wide social circle, and you often get news and opportunities through them. Your connections are your treasure. While being generous with friends, also look after your own time and wallet, and give only what you can.
palaces.官祿: With Hua Lu in the Career Palace, you tend to meet good opportunities and collaborators at work, get results, and enjoy it more. Once you find a direction you like, keep digging deeper, and the rewards will become more and more visible.
palaces.田宅: With Hua Lu in the Property Palace, your home feels warm, and you have a better chance of building up a place to settle. Living comfortably is your foundation. Keeping your home running smoothly adds to both your mood and how you work.
palaces.福德: With Hua Lu in the Well-being Palace, you know how to find enjoyment, you are optimistic, you don't easily dwell on things, and you can often lift your own mood. This ease is your greatest asset. Protect it, and don't let busyness wear it away.
palaces.父母: With Hua Lu in the Parents Palace, you get along well with elders and bosses, often receive care and support from them, and feel little pressure around them. When problems come up, asking those with more experience will be much faster than feeling your way alone.

minor.左輔: Zuo Fu is a helper star. It means people around you are willing to lend a hand. In whichever palace it sits, that area makes it easier to find helpers. Remember to ask when you need to.
minor.右弼: You Bi is also a helper star, but its help is more subtle and more private than Zuo Fu's. Often someone quietly fills the gap for you before you even ask.
minor.文昌: Wen Chang stands for study, exams, and paperwork skills, and it helps you work in an orderly way. When you need to write something or sit for a certification, it is a good helper.
minor.文曲: Wen Qu stands for eloquence, talent in the arts, and inspiration, and it helps you express yourself vividly and charmingly. It suits getting your ideas across through speaking, performing, or creating.
minor.天魁: Tian Kui is a star of helpful people, who mostly come from elders, bosses, or formal settings. When something important comes up, asking a senior for advice often brings useful guidance.
minor.天鉞: Tian Yue is also a star of helpful people, who mostly appear through private introductions or chance encounters. Stay in touch with people. Opportunities often come out of casual chats.
minor.祿存: Lu Cun stands for steady resources and the ability to hold on to what you have. It makes you careful and good at saving. It suits a slow, steady stream and does not suit going all in at once.
minor.天馬: Tian Ma stands for movement and change, and it often brings chances for business trips, moves, or new environments. Getting moving tends to open things up, so don't be afraid of change.
minor.擎羊: The friction of Qing Yang comes from rushing too fast and speaking too bluntly, so things easily turn into head-on clashes. The way around it is to set your feelings down before you act, and to say the same thing in a better way.
minor.陀羅: The friction of Tuo Luo comes from delay and going back and forth in hesitation, so things easily get stuck halfway. The way around it is to break big matters into small steps and push a little each day.
minor.火星: The friction of Huo Xing comes from impatience, making decisions on a sudden impulse. The way around it is to sleep on important matters before replying, and to take a deep breath before acting on urgent ones.
minor.鈴星: The friction of Ling Xing comes from keeping things bottled up until feelings built up over time suddenly burst out. The way around it is to speak up early when something bothers you, or to find an outlet to release the pressure.
minor.地空: The friction of Di Kong comes from having many ideas that never land, so plans easily spin in place. The way around it is to pick the smallest version and actually make it first, then adjust little by little.
minor.地劫: Di Jie's friction is that things often hit surprises you didn't expect, and your effort doesn't go the way you planned. The way around it is to keep a backup plan and not put all your resources in at once.

命宮.plain: The annual Life Palace has returned to your natal Life Palace, so this year centers on you. You'll want to be clearer about what you want and what suits you, and you'll have more energy to start fresh. It's a good time to take out a plan you've set aside for a long while and set a direction for the next few years. Don't rush to fit around other people. Find your own pace first.
命宮.ask_next: What is the one thing you most want to see through for yourself this year?

兄弟.plain: The annual Life Palace falls in your natal Siblings Palace, so this year you'll deal more with siblings, peers, and business partners. Someone may ask you to work on something together, or you may need to sort out who does what or how money moves between you. Say things plainly and keep clear accounts, and the partnership can run smoothly.
兄弟.ask_next: Which partner or family member do you most want to sit down and talk with this year?

夫妻.plain: The annual Life Palace falls in your natal Spouse Palace, so love and partnership are the focus this year. If you're single, you have a better chance of meeting someone new. If you're with someone, you'll talk more often about your future together. This is a good year to lay out your expectations and who does what, and talk them through.
夫妻.ask_next: In love, what is the one thing you most want to get clear on this year?

子女.plain: The annual Life Palace falls in your natal Children Palace, so this year your mind is often on younger people, students, or your own creative work. You may train newcomers, start a creative project, or give more of yourself to the children at home. It's also a good year to pick up a new interest and add more enjoyment to life.
子女.ask_next: Which person or piece of work do you most want to put your energy into this year?

財帛.plain: The annual Life Palace falls in your natal Wealth Palace, so money and income are the focus this year. You'll pay more attention to how you earn, save, and spend, and a new source of income may appear. Get your income and spending in order and set clear goals. What you arrange this year can shape the next several years.
財帛.ask_next: With money, which one thing do you most want to handle first this year?

疾厄.plain: The annual Life Palace falls in your natal Health Palace, so this year is a good time to bring your focus back to daily rhythm and managing stress. When things pile up, your body and mind will give you signals, so don't ignore them. Setting regular times for rest and exercise works better than pushing through on willpower.
疾厄.ask_next: This year, do you most want to adjust your daily routine or the pace you work at?

遷移.plain: The annual Life Palace falls in your natal Travel Palace, so this year brings many chances to go out and change things up. You may take a business trip, travel, move, or change your surroundings, and you're likely to meet new people and opportunities along the way. Loosen up a little and get out more. You'll often come back with unexpected gains and inspiration.
遷移.ask_next: Is there a place you've long wanted to go to, or to move to?

交友.plain: The annual Life Palace falls in your natal Friends Palace, so relationships are the focus this year, and friends, colleagues, and clients will all have an influence. As your network grows, you'll also see more clearly who can be a lasting presence in your life. Go to more gatherings, but keep some time for yourself.
交友.ask_next: Which relationship do you most want to get closer to this year, or keep more distance from?

官祿.plain: The annual Life Palace falls in your natal Career Palace, so work and career are the main thread this year. You may get a new assignment, change jobs, or be given more responsibility in your current role. Your effort is easily noticed this year, so take the chance to show what you can do, and remember to look after your pace.
官祿.ask_next: At work, how far do you most want to move forward this year?

田宅.plain: The annual Life Palace falls in your natal Property Palace, so home and living space are the focus this year. You may think about moving, tidy up your place, or spend more time with family. Make your home a place where you feel at ease and want to relax when you come back, and other things tend to settle too.
田宅.ask_next: What part of your home do you most want to work on first this year?

福德.plain: The annual Life Palace falls in your natal Well-being Palace, so this year centers on your mood and quality of life. You'll want to be more comfortable and do what you enjoy, and you may rethink what really makes you happy. It's a good time to build a hobby or learn something new, giving your mind a place to rest.
福德.ask_next: What could really help you relax and catch your breath this year?

父母.plain: The annual Life Palace falls in your natal Parents Palace, so this year you'll have more dealings with elders, supervisors, and government offices. You may need to spend more time with older family members, or communicate more with those above you at work. Paperwork and procedures may also bunch up this year. Just handle them with care.
父母.ask_next: What do you most want to talk through with an elder or a supervisor this year?

monthly.命宮: This month the monthly period reaches the Life Palace, and your attention turns back to yourself. It's a good time to sort out your thoughts, check your recent pace, and set a small goal for the next month or two.
monthly.兄弟: This month you have more contact with siblings, colleagues, and partners, and you can talk things over together. When work division or money is involved, be sure to say it clearly beforehand to avoid awkwardness later.
monthly.夫妻: This month matters of the heart stir your mood more. If you're with someone, spend more time together and talk about how you each are doing. If you're single, pay attention to new connections around you.
monthly.子女: This month your mind easily turns to younger people, students, or creative work, so it's a good time to start a small new project. If you have children at home, you can also make time to do something with them.
monthly.財帛: This month money stands out, and both income and spending may shift a bit. It's a good time to check your accounts, see which expenses you could cut, and adjust your budget for the coming months.
monthly.疾厄: This month pay special attention to your daily rhythm, since you tire easily when things pile up. Going to bed earlier and leaving gaps in your schedule to rest works better than rushing to keep up, and you're less likely to get stuck.
monthly.遷移: This month brings many chances to go out and move around. You may take a business trip, run errands outside, or plan a trip. You're likely to meet new people out there, so chat a bit more, as you often pick up unexpected news.
monthly.交友: This month is busy with social activity, with more gatherings of friends and work dinners. Besides the new information that exchange brings, leave yourself some time alone and don't pack your schedule too full.
monthly.官祿: Work is the focus this month, and a new task or a busy project may land in your hands. Focus on doing what's in front of you well and delivering on time, and you're likely to be noticed.
monthly.田宅: This month there's more going on at home, so it's a good time to tidy up your place and deal with chores you've put off for a long time. You can also spend a little more time having a meal with family to warm the mood at home.
monthly.福德: This month is a good time to slow down and do something that makes you happy: read a book, go for a walk, or rest early. When your mood is good, everything else goes more smoothly too.
monthly.父母: This month you communicate more with elders and supervisors, and paperwork and procedures may come all at once. Look things over once more before you send them and check carefully, and you'll get through fine.

intro: Zi Wei Dou Shu uses the year, month, day, and hour of birth to lay out a chart that looks at life through twelve palaces. The Life Palace speaks of who you are. The other eleven speak of siblings, relationships, children, money, daily rhythm, going out, friends, work, home, mood, and elders. Each palace holds different stars, and the stars' traits together with the Four Transformations make up how you show up in that area. Once your chart is laid out, you can start with the Life Palace and Body Palace to understand yourself, then open the palaces you care about and read them slowly. To see the focus of these years or this year, look at the decade and the annual period. A chart describes tendencies and habits. It doesn't decide the outcome, and how you go is still your own choice.

faq.q: What if I don't know my birth hour?
faq.a: Zi Wei Dou Shu needs the birth hour to place the Life Palace, and a different hour changes the palaces of the whole chart. You can start by asking family or looking for the record on your birth certificate or your mother's maternity handbook. If you really can't find it, pick the most likely hour and lay out the chart, treating what you read as a reference. Or look at the BaZi three pillars (year, month and day — no hour pillar), which don't need the hour.

The clock we normally use is shared across a whole time zone, but the moment the sun actually reaches its midday point differs with the longitude of the birthplace. True solar time is the time with that difference corrected. When the birth time falls close to the boundary between two double-hours, whether you correct it may change where the Life Palace lands.

faq.q: How do I lay out a chart for someone born in a Chinese lunar calendar leap month?
faq.a: A leap month has no month position of its own. A common approach is to split it in two: the first half (day 1 to 15) counts as the current month, and the second half (day 16 onward) counts as the next month. Other approaches count the whole leap month as the current month, or all of it as the next month. Different approaches produce different charts, so be sure to check which one is used.

faq.q: Why is my chart different from other websites?
faq.a: Zi Wei Dou Shu is practiced differently in a few places: whether to correct to true solar time, whether the day changes at midnight or at 11 p.m. during the Zi hour, how a leap month is assigned, and which version of the Four Transformations is used. If even one of these differs, the charts can differ. When you compare results, first check that these settings match, then look at the chart.

The Body Palace is a second palace on the chart that relates to "you." It is set by your birth month and birth hour, and it overlaps with the Life Palace or one of the other palaces. The Life Palace is more like your natural temperament. The Body Palace is more like what you come to care about and put yourself into as you live. As you get older, the matters of the Body Palace usually become more important.

The Four Transformations are Hua Lu, Hua Quan, Hua Ke, and Hua Ji. They are set by the Heavenly Stem of your birth year, and each attaches to one of four stars. Hua Lu is like resources flowing in. Hua Quan is drive and taking the lead. Hua Ke is reputation and helpful people. Hua Ji is where you put the most thought. Seeing which palace each one lands in shows which parts of your life you feel most strongly.

faq.q: What are the decade and the annual period?
faq.a: The decade is a ten-year period. Every ten years a different palace becomes the focus, giving you the broad direction of that stretch. The annual period is the change from year to year, and each year one palace serves as that year's Life Palace. Look at the decade first to see what the ten years are busy with, then at the annual period for this year's focus. Reading the two together is clearer.

faq.q: What should I watch for if I was born in the Zi hour?
faq.a: The Zi hour runs from 11 p.m. to 1 a.m., so it spans two days. For people born between 11 p.m. and midnight, some methods count that as the same day and others as the next day. A common approach is to change the day at 11 p.m. Whether the day changes affects your birth date, and the whole chart may change with it. If you were born in the Zi hour, pay close attention to which method is used when the chart is set up.

紫微|命宮.title: Has own views, used to standing in the center
紫微|命宮.plain: With Zi Wei in your Life Palace, the first impression you give is often steady and measured. You don't say much, but what you say carries weight. You hold yourself to your own standards, want things to move at your own pace, and are willing to take on responsibility. When others can't decide something, they often glance your way without thinking. You care about face and about principles. When you feel respected, you give a lot. When you feel brushed off, you say nothing outwardly but remember it for a long time. You do best when you have people to talk things over with and to fill the gaps for you.
紫微|命宮.strength: When people trust you and give you room to lead, you can keep a group steady. You take responsibility for your decisions, and the bigger the occasion, the calmer you stay.
紫微|命宮.watch: You can get stuck when you can't set your pride aside and keep questions to yourself. When something is unfamiliar, asking one question first takes much less effort than pushing through alone.
紫微|命宮.ask_next: What do you most want to decide for yourself right now: your position at work, or a choice in your daily life?

紫微|兄弟.title: Keeps a sense of measure with siblings and peers
紫微|兄弟.plain: With siblings and close peers, you tend to each have your own sky. With Zi Wei in the Siblings Palace, they may be strong-willed and have their own views. You respect each other but don't stick together much. In big moments, they are often the ones who can hold things up, though you may not be in touch often day to day. At work, colleagues at your level are also often capable people with a temper. Whether you work well together depends on who is willing to give way first.
紫微|兄弟.strength: When you appreciate each other, your peers are a weighty backing for you. At a key moment, one phone call can help, and their word counts.
紫微|兄弟.watch: When both sides like to take charge, small things can get stuck. Settle who handles which part, then follow through. It cuts a lot of tug-of-war, and both sides keep their face.
紫微|兄弟.ask_next: With siblings or peers, do you want to get closer, or to state your boundaries clearly?

紫微|夫妻.title: Wants a partner worth admiring
紫微|夫妻.plain: With Zi Wei in the Spouse Palace, you have expectations of a partner. You want someone capable and presentable, someone you can bring out in public and who can support you when you need it. You may be drawn to people with a strong presence and their own views. In the relationship, your partner often has firm convictions, and you both care about face. Once things settle, you're like partners running a home together. What you give each other is respect and dignity, not the sweetness of being together every day.
紫微|夫妻.strength: When you affirm each other, you are each other's best face to the world. You work well together on outside matters, and the relationship lasts. Even outsiders look on with envy.
紫微|夫妻.watch: You can get stuck on who listens to whom. In an argument, set aside winning and ask, "What do you really care about?" It often helps more than reasoning.
紫微|夫妻.ask_next: In love, what matters most to you: being respected, or feeling cared for?

紫微|子女.title: Invests in the next generation, and can be a bit strict
紫微|子女.plain: When it comes to children, students, or newcomers you mentor, you carry a hope that they will make something of themselves and walk a straight path. With Zi Wei in the Children Palace, you are willing to put resources into nurturing them, and you may unconsciously set the bar higher. The children often have their own personality and views and don't like being arranged, so the harder you push, the more they want to do it themselves. This palace also relates to your creative work and what you make yourself. You like producing results with quality that you're proud to show.
紫微|子女.strength: The support you give carries weight. When younger people feel valued, they are glad to aim higher and produce results that make you proud. There is also more of an understanding between you.
紫微|子女.watch: You can end up managing too much and deciding for them. Ask how they want to do it first, then add your advice. The relationship loosens up, and they can take it in more easily.
紫微|子女.ask_next: What is on your mind most right now: a child's or junior's direction, or your own work in hand?

紫微|財帛.title: Values quality in spending, and values control too
紫微|財帛.plain: With Zi Wei in the Wealth Palace, you look at money in a more generous but more particular way: you would rather buy less but buy well. You like to manage your own finances and don't much like others interfering in how you spend. For earning, a path with a position and a reputation driving income suits you. Money that comes from expertise or rank is usually steadier than money that comes from luck. Sometimes you pay a bit more for the occasion, and afterward you still find it worthwhile, because it's the dignity you care about.
紫微|財帛.strength: With a clear goal, you hold the big picture well. You spend what should be spent and keep what should be kept, and your finances grow in scale. You are not easily carried away by a passing mood.
紫微|財帛.watch: You can overspend for face and find it hard to say no. Before a large expense, give yourself a day before deciding. You'll feel more settled and less likely to regret it afterward.
紫微|財帛.ask_next: About money, what do you most want to work out: how to earn more, or how to hold on to it?

紫微|疾厄.title: Tends to carry stress alone without saying
紫微|疾厄.plain: You handle stress by holding up. However much there is to do, you stay steady on the surface and rarely let people see you're tired. With Zi Wei in the Health Palace, you put responsibility first and rest last. Often you finish a big stretch and only then realize you ran out long ago. Your rhythm suits a regular routine: sleeping at a set time and stopping at a set time helps more than an occasional big catch-up. Having time to put down your roles matters especially for you.
紫微|疾厄.strength: You have good endurance. When your routine is steady, your energy and stamina can carry long, big tasks, and you recover quickly. You can also keep a good state for a long time.
紫微|疾厄.watch: You can push on until the last moment before stopping. Leave a small stretch each day when you handle nothing at all. It works better than one long sleep on the weekend.
紫微|疾厄.ask_next: Lately, does your stress come more from too much responsibility, or too little rest?

紫微|遷移.title: Gets noticed once out the door
紫微|遷移.plain: With Zi Wei in the Travel Palace, you often carry more weight outside than at home. When you go out on business, travel to other places, or move into a new environment, you tend to meet people willing to lift you up, and you're more likely to be put in the spotlight. Others see you as reliable and impressive. This placement also hints that chances usually come more from going out than from staying put. But outside there is more face and more roles to keep up, so when you get home you especially want quiet.
紫微|遷移.strength: When you change environments or build something away from home, you can hold the stage well. Helpful people and opportunities often appear in other places or new circles. Going out can even show you your own weight more clearly.
紫微|遷移.watch: Outside, you can focus only on your image and not say when you're tired. Before filling up your schedule, leave yourself some room to breathe. Before going home, let yourself really put down the role.
紫微|遷移.ask_next: Are you thinking about whether to go somewhere new or into a new environment to build your path?

紫微|交友.title: Often has capable people in the friend circle
紫微|交友.plain: The friends, coworkers, and partners around you are often capable people with minds of their own. With Zi Wei in the Friends Palace, you can learn a lot from them and draw on their help. But these people are usually used to making the calls themselves, and they won't always go about things your way. You're picky about friendships and would rather have a few that carry weight. On a team, you may notice that you're not the only one moving things forward. Learning to share the work with these people is more effective than rushing ahead alone.
紫微|交友.strength: You're good at meeting people of substance. When you need resources or opinions, there's usually someone nearby who can give you sound advice and real help.
紫微|交友.watch: When friends have strong opinions, it's easy to get swept along. On important matters, listen to what they say, then ask yourself again what you want to do. The final call is still yours.
紫微|交友.ask_next: In your social life right now, do you want to meet more people, or sort out the circle you already have?

紫微|官祿.title: Suited to a seat where you make the calls
紫微|官祿.plain: With Zi Wei in the Career Palace, work is a stage you care about a great deal. You work with vision, like to hold the whole picture, and want your role to be seen and respected. Rather than only carrying out tasks, you're better suited to being the person in charge, leading projects, or building expertise to the point where others come to you for advice. You may need to put in a stretch of hard work at the start, but once you're in the right position, you grow steadier over time. You hold high standards for your work and are willing to take on extra pressure for results.
紫微|官祿.strength: When you're given responsibility, you can carry a task from start to finish. You decide decisively, and your team is willing to follow you. Your position also grows steadier over time.
紫微|官祿.watch: You may want to decide everything yourself, leaving the people under you no room to step in. Try handing off some of the work, and you'll have more time to look at the big picture.
紫微|官祿.ask_next: At work right now, are you waiting for a chance to move up, or thinking about whether to change stages?

紫微|田宅.title: A home needs to feel right to feel safe
紫微|田宅.plain: The feeling of "home" matters a lot to you. With Zi Wei in the Property Palace, you want a place that is spacious, tidy, and a little stately, one where you at least feel like the master of the house when you come back. You care about the quality of where you live and would rather spend a bit more to be comfortable. The mood at home often centers on an elder or on you, and someone makes the big decisions. This palace also relates to your attitude toward houses and family assets. You lean toward steady accumulation and aren't in a hurry to chase.
紫微|田宅.strength: When home feels right, your mind settles too. However much is going on outside, you can recharge once you're back. Your family also feels at ease because of you.
紫微|田宅.watch: You may feel the need to manage everything at home. Give the people you live with a corner of their own and some say in decisions, and the atmosphere at home will feel much lighter.
紫微|田宅.ask_next: What's on your mind lately: moving, tidying up your living space, or how people at home get along?

紫微|福德.title: A pride inside that you don't easily voice
紫微|福德.plain: With Zi Wei in the Well-being Palace, your inner world is more particular than it looks from the outside. You have standards for the quality of life, like well-made things and conversations with depth, and you need a little time alone to sort yourself out. You have real self-respect and don't like letting others see you vulnerable. What truly makes you happy is often not liveliness, but the satisfaction of "I chose this myself and did it properly," which is quiet but very solid.
紫微|福德.strength: When your mood is steady, you can enjoy your own company. Thinking quietly, you often come up with directions that have real weight. That certainty also earns the trust of people around you.
紫微|福德.watch: You may think too much without saying it, going in circles inside. Talking with someone you trust is usually faster than working it out alone. Once you say it aloud, half the weight often lifts.
紫微|福德.ask_next: What's weighing on you most lately: a situation, or a person?

紫微|父母.title: Elders give you weight and expectations
紫微|父母.plain: Your parents or main elders are often people with strong views who have the final word at home. With Zi Wei in the Parents Palace, what they give you may be a good starting point, or it may be a sizable expectation. At work, this palace also relates to your bosses and superiors, and you're likely to meet capable bosses with presence. If you respect their position when dealing with them, you can gain a lot of practical support and guidance from them.
紫微|父母.strength: When things go smoothly with elders and bosses, you often receive promotion or resources. Someone opens a door for you and your path goes faster. You also learn a lot about how to carry yourself and handle things.
紫微|父母.watch: You may feel controlled or asked for too much. First hear what the other person is really worried about, then share your view. That works better than pushing back head-on.
紫微|父母.ask_next: Is there something you want to say to an elder or boss but haven't yet?

天機|命宮.title: A quick mind that can't sit still
天機|命宮.plain: With Tian Ji in your Life Palace, what stands out most is that your mind never stops. You react fast and have plenty of ideas. You like looking for causes and solutions, and while others are still stunned, you've already thought of three approaches. You suit work that involves thinking, planning, and analysis, and you're good at finding a way through change. But with so much thinking, your heart gets busy too. Sometimes before you've started, you've already run through everything that could go wrong, and that tires you out.
天機|命宮.strength: When a problem needs brainpower, you come alive. You quickly grasp the key point and offer methods others hadn't thought of. The more complex the problem, the more you enjoy it.
天機|命宮.watch: You may overthink and keep revising. Pick one direction, work on it for a short stretch, and adjust as you go. That takes less effort than rehearsing in your head.
天機|命宮.ask_next: Which undecided matter has been running through your mind the most lately?

天機|兄弟.title: Among peers, you connect through ideas
天機|兄弟.plain: Your siblings or close peers are more like partners you can talk ideas with. With Tian Ji in the Siblings Palace, they may be smart and quick, often offering you a different angle. But your lives change a lot, so sometimes you're very close and sometimes you're each busy and out of touch for a while. At work, peers at your level are mostly sharp-minded too. Ideas flow when you collaborate, but the risk is too much discussion and too few people actually doing.
天機|兄弟.strength: When you're stuck, talking with them often sets you straight. Reminding each other and trading ideas helps a lot. Many things find their answer as you talk.
天機|兄弟.watch: With so many ideas, people can end up talking past each other. After a discussion, wrap it up: who does what, and by when. Writing it down keeps it from falling apart, and lets everyone see progress.
天機|兄弟.ask_next: Is there something you'd really like to talk over with a sibling or peer?

天機|夫妻.title: In love, you need someone you can talk with
天機|夫妻.plain: With Tian Ji in the Spouse Palace, you value whether you can really talk with someone in love. More than looks, you're drawn to people who are smart, thoughtful, and quick. Together you have plenty to talk about and often discuss things, but you both have many thoughts and sensitive minds, so a single remark can set you thinking a lot. The rhythm of the relationship may shift often, and it takes time to find a pace you're both comfortable with. Once it settles, you'll be each other's best sounding board.
天機|夫妻.strength: When love goes well, you're like teammates, working things out and planning life together, and your partner understands what's going on in your head.
天機|夫妻.watch: You may build a whole storyline from one sentence. If you have a question, ask directly, and don't let guesses answer for the other person. One extra question often saves days of overthinking.
天機|夫妻.ask_next: In love, what do you turn over most: the other person's feelings, or your future together?

天機|子女.title: The younger generation is bright and changeable
天機|子女.plain: Your children, students, or the newcomers you guide are often quick-minded and very curious. With Tian Ji in the Children Palace, they have many ideas and their interests change easily: learning this today, trying that tomorrow. With them you're more like teacher and friend, and reasoning and discussion work better than orders. This palace also relates to your creative output. Ideas keep coming when you make things, though you often start several at once.
天機|子女.strength: You're good at inspiring younger people. One sentence from you points a direction and they can think onward by themselves, so the relationship stays easy and relaxed. They may also see you as someone they can open up to.
天機|子女.watch: When the younger ones keep changing, you may get anxious along with them. Give them a set period to try one thing, and talk about switching only after that. Let them learn to carry something through to a stopping point.
天機|子女.ask_next: Right now, would you rather understand your child's learning direction, or your own creative plans?

天機|財帛.title: Earning through your mind and planning
天機|財帛.plain: Most of your income probably comes from using your head. Work that runs on ideas, like planning, analysis, technical work, or consulting, is more likely to bring you money. With Tian Ji (a main star) in the Wealth Palace, you're good at figuring out money and like studying how to save and how to divide it up. But your income may not come at a steady pace. Some times are fuller, some thinner, and your mood can rise and fall with it. Before spending, you often compare prices and think for a long while, yet now and then you act on impulse because something seems like a good deal.
天機|財帛.strength: You're good at planning a budget and finding smarter ways to spend. Where your money goes is usually clear in your mind and doesn't easily get muddled. Sudden expenses rarely throw you off.
天機|財帛.watch: With so many ideas, you may switch money methods too quickly. Pick one simple method and stick with it for half a year, then decide whether to adjust. A simple method kept up for a long time often works best.
天機|財帛.ask_next: When you think about money these days, is it more about whether your income is steady, or about how to divide it up?

天機|疾厄.title: When your mind gets busy, your routine falls apart
天機|疾厄.plain: With Tian Ji (a main star) in the Health Palace (read only as daily rhythm and pace), your stress mostly comes from a mind that won't stop. You think about things all day, and when you lie down at night you're still thinking, so sleep and rest often get taken over by your thoughts. Your rhythm easily rises and falls with whatever is changing, so when you're busy you forget to eat, and when you're idle you feel empty. What matters most for you is finding a way to switch your head off: a regular bedtime habit, a short walk, or writing tomorrow's tasks on paper so your mind can let go.
天機|疾厄.strength: You adjust quickly. As soon as you notice your routine slipping, you're willing to change your approach right away, and once you find a rhythm that suits you, you bounce back well. Your daily rhythm tends to get back on track with it.
天機|疾厄.watch: At bedtime you can easily keep scrolling on your phone or turning things over in your mind. Before turning off the light, write down what you need to do tomorrow, and your mind settles more easily. You may also wake up feeling fresher.
天機|疾厄.ask_next: What has bothered you more lately: not sleeping well, or resting and still feeling tired?

天機|遷移.title: Going out makes your mind sharper
天機|遷移.plain: Going out, traveling, or changing your surroundings often brings you fresh inspiration and helps you work out things you couldn't figure out at home. With Tian Ji (a main star) in the Travel Palace, you're especially energetic when you're out in the world, and you may often need to move around, or have work that keeps you on the road. Out there, you come across as smart, quick, and good at adapting. But changing settings too often can also leave you feeling rootless, so you need a place where you can settle.
天機|遷移.strength: In a new environment you adapt very fast. You size up the situation and find your way in quickly, and good opportunities often come to you away from home. You often find shortcuts faster than the locals do.
天機|遷移.watch: At the first sign of trouble, you may want to move somewhere else. Before you do, ask yourself whether the problem is the place, or whether you want to escape what's in front of you. Think it through before you move, and your next stop will fit better.
天機|遷移.ask_next: Do you want a change of scene because you want to explore, or because you want to leave how things are now?

天機|交友.title: Your friends are mostly idea people
天機|交友.plain: With Tian Ji (a main star) in the Friends Palace, the friends and colleagues around you tend to be sharp and well informed. Your conversations are full of information, and you often trade ideas and leads. But friends like this come and go, and your circle changes quickly. Some people are close for a while, then fade. In teamwork, everyone has plenty of ideas, so you may need to be the one who narrows the direction and decides the next step, so the discussion actually lands somewhere.
天機|交友.strength: You easily pick up new information and new ways of doing things from your friends. Whatever you want to do, someone can give you a good idea. Your exchanges with them often bring new opportunities too.
天機|交友.watch: Your circle changes fast, so you may feel you can't hold on to anything. Choose a few people you really connect with and keep in regular touch, and your relationships will be much steadier. Old friends are often your best reassurance.
天機|交友.ask_next: Would you rather meet new friends, or get back in touch with old ones?

天機|官祿.title: Suited to work that uses your head and keeps changing
天機|官祿.plain: Your strengths at work are planning and adapting. With Tian Ji (a main star) in the Career Palace, work that involves analysis, planning, research, and problem solving lets you shine most. You don't much like things staying the same, and you feel bored when you do something too repetitive for too long. Your career may change direction a few times, and each change is really you looking for a position that suits your mind better. You're well suited to being the one behind the scenes who comes up with ideas, or the one who proposes the plan.
天機|官祿.strength: When you meet a complicated problem, you can break it into steps and propose a workable plan. You're the kind of mind a team really needs. Many thorny matters start to make sense once they reach your hands.
天機|官祿.watch: You may make many plans while follow-through lags behind. After each round of planning, pick the smallest step and do it right away to get things moving. Once you have a bit of a result, you'll have more drive to keep going.
天機|官祿.ask_next: At work right now, do you want to change tracks, or find a new way of doing things where you are?

天機|田宅.title: Your living situation often changes or gets adjusted
天機|田宅.plain: Your connection with the places you live tends to involve change. You may have moved a few times, or often want to rearrange things at home. With Tian Ji (a main star) in the Property Palace, you have many ideas about living space and like making your home more convenient and efficient. The mood at home is lively, with lots of talk and lots of opinions. This palace also reminds you that home is where your mind gets to rest, and changing it too often can make it harder for you to truly relax.
天機|田宅.strength: You make good use of space. Even a small place can be planned to work well, and when you move to a new home you settle your life in quickly. You can always make your home work more smoothly.
天機|田宅.watch: You may keep wanting to change and swap things, so home always feels like a construction site. Decide on one corner to leave as it is, so you have a steady place to rest.
天機|田宅.ask_next: What's on your mind: moving, reorganizing, or how people at home communicate?

天機|福德.title: A careful heart that likes to think things through
天機|福德.plain: You have a rich inner life. You like reading, researching, and working through questions, and you're curious about many things. With Tian Ji (a main star) in the Well-being Palace, you find enjoyment in thinking, and you don't get bored when you're alone. But a delicate mind can also overthink. A small matter circles in your head several times and stirs up your mood. You need a way to quiet your mind, such as making something with your hands or exercising regularly, so your head can switch channels for a while.
天機|福德.strength: You're good at finding your own fun. Learning something new or digging into a topic you're interested in quickly recharges you. That pleasure in learning is an important source of nourishment for you.
